rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem:
When a mixture of baking soda and tartaric acid is heated (or mixed in water) a product ‘X’ is formed, which is responsible for making breads and cakes soft and spongy.

The product ‘X’ is
rows.solution:
Baking powder is baking soda mixed with a mild edible acid such as tartaric acid. When it is heated or mixed with water, the hydrogencarbonate reacts with the acid and gives off carbon dioxide:

\(\mathrm{NaHCO_3 + H^+ \rightarrow CO_2 + H_2O + Na^+}\) (from the acid)

The carbon dioxide gas makes the dough rise, so breads and cakes become soft and spongy.

This is option (A) Carbon dioxide.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem:
Consider the following ray diagram :

Here, the angle of incidence and angle of deviation respectively are
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - a triangular glass prism with a ray entering its left face and emerging from its right face; dashed normals at both faces, the incident ray produced forward and the emergent ray produced backward as dashed lines, and six angles marked a, b, c, d, e and f. Which angle lies between which lines exists only in the drawing and is withheld here, since it is the answer. Page idx 10.
rows.solution:
The angle of incidence is the angle between the incident ray and the normal at the first face of the prism. In the figure that is angle b; angle a is between the incident ray and the face itself.

The angle of deviation is the angle between the incident ray produced forward and the emergent ray produced backward. In the figure that is angle e, marked where the two dashed lines meet above the ray inside the prism.

This is option (C) b and e.

rows.stem:
During an experiment, a student observes that the given mirror is forming an erect and diminished image for all positions of the object placed in front of it.

Based on the this information, answer the following questions :

(a) Identify the mirror.

(b) Using new Cartesian sign convention, write the magnitude of the magnification in this case.

(c) What will be the radius of curvature of the mirror if its focal length is 20 cm ?
rows.solution:
(a) The mirror is a convex mirror. It is the only mirror that forms an erect, diminished image for every position of the object.

(b) The image is virtual and erect, so by the new Cartesian sign convention the magnification is positive; the image is diminished, so the magnification is less than 1. That is, \(0 < m < 1\).

(c) \(R = 2f = 2 \times 20 = 40\) cm. With the sign convention, the focal length of a convex mirror is \(+20\) cm, so \(R = +40\) cm.

rows.stem: Determine the maximum and minimum resistance which can be obtained by joining five resistors of \(\frac{1}{5}\,\Omega\) each.
rows.solution:
The resistance is maximum when all five resistors are joined in series:

\(R_s = 5 \times \dfrac{1}{5} = 1\,\Omega\).

The resistance is minimum when all five are joined in parallel:

\(\dfrac{1}{R_p} = \dfrac{1}{1/5} + \dfrac{1}{1/5} + \dfrac{1}{1/5} + \dfrac{1}{1/5} + \dfrac{1}{1/5} = 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 25\), so \(R_p = \dfrac{1}{25}\,\Omega = 0{\cdot}04\,\Omega\).

rows.stem: Calculate potential difference across a \(4\,\Omega\) resistor that produces 100 J of heat every second.
rows.solution:
Heat produced \(H = 100\) J in \(t = 1\) s, and \(R = 4\,\Omega\).

\(H = \dfrac{V^2 t}{R}\), so \(V = \sqrt{\dfrac{HR}{t}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{100 \times 4}{1}} = \sqrt{400} = 20\) V.

Check: the current is \(I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{20}{4} = 5\) A, and \(I^2R = 25 \times 4 = 100\) W, which is 100 J every second.

rows.stem:
Study the food web given below :

(a) Identify the food chain(s) in which the eagle receives the highest energy from the producers.

(b) Identify the organism in which a non-biodegradable pesticide will be found in maximum concentration. Name the term used for this phenomenon.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the food web exists only in the drawing: pictures labelled Grass, Grass Hopper, Mouse, Mongoose, Frog, Snake and Eagle, joined by arrows. Which organism feeds on which is what both parts ask about and is withheld here. Page idx 16.
rows.solution:
(a) Only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level passes to the next, so the eagle receives the most energy from the producers through the shortest food chains. In this web those are the two three-step chains:

Grass \(\rightarrow\) Mouse \(\rightarrow\) Eagle

Grass \(\rightarrow\) Mongoose \(\rightarrow\) Eagle

(b) The eagle, at the top of the food web, will have the maximum concentration of a non-biodegradable pesticide. The pesticide is not broken down, so it accumulates at each trophic level and its concentration increases up the chain. This is called biological magnification.

rows.stem: A copper wire on burning in flame, gets coated with a black substance. Write the chemical equation of the reaction that takes place. How can this chemical change be reversed ?
rows.solution:
On heating, copper combines with oxygen of the air to form black copper(II) oxide:

\(\mathrm{2Cu + O_2 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2CuO}\)

The change is reversed by passing hydrogen gas over the heated copper oxide. The black coating turns brown again as copper is formed:

\(\mathrm{CuO + H_2 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} Cu + H_2O}\)

rows.stem:
Answer the following questions for a case in which a current carrying conductor is placed in a uniform magnetic field :

(a) List three factors on which the magnitude of the force acting on the conductor depends.

(b) When is the magnitude of force on the conductor maximum ?

(c) Name the rule which helps in determining the direction of force on the conductor and give its one application.
rows.solution:
(a) Any three: the magnitude of the current in the conductor; the strength of the magnetic field; the length of the conductor; the orientation of the conductor with respect to the magnetic field.

(b) The force is maximum when the conductor (the direction of the current) is at right angles to the direction of the magnetic field.

(c) Fleming's left-hand rule: stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of the current, the thumb points in the direction of the force (motion) on the conductor.

Application: the electric motor. (The marking scheme also accepts microphones and generators here. A generator, however, works by electromagnetic induction, and the direction of its induced current is given by Fleming's right-hand rule, so the electric motor is the safe answer.)

rows.stem: Differentiate between self-pollination and cross pollination. Which one of the two is better for the survival of species ? Give reason to justify your answer.
rows.solution:
| Self-pollination | Cross-pollination |
|---|---|
| Pollen grains are transferred from the stamen to the stigma of the same flower | Pollen grains are transferred from the stamen of one flower to the stigma of another flower of the same species |

Cross-pollination is better for the survival of the species. It brings together the DNA of two different plants, which creates more variation in the offspring, and variation helps some individuals survive when the environment changes.

rows.stem: List three raw materials required by terrestrial plants for photosynthesis. Explain how nature provides these raw material to the plants.
rows.solution:
The three raw materials are carbon dioxide, water and light (sunlight).

Carbon dioxide: taken in from the atmosphere through the stomata of the leaves.

Water: absorbed from the soil by the roots and carried up to the leaves through the xylem.

Light: comes from the sun and is absorbed by the chlorophyll in the leaves.

rows.stem:
(a) Define the term “Functional group of a carbon compound”. Write the formula of functional group present in (i) propanol and (ii) propanone.

(b) Name the process of conversion of (i) ethanol to ethene and (ii) ethanol to ethanoic acid. Write the reaction equation stating the conditions required for each of the reactions to occur.
rows.solution:
(a) A functional group is an atom or a group of atoms (a heteroatom such as oxygen or a halogen, or a group containing one) that replaces hydrogen in a hydrocarbon chain and gives the compound its characteristic chemical properties, whatever the length of the chain.

(i) Propanol: the alcohol group, \(-\mathrm{OH}\).

(ii) Propanone: the ketone group, \(-\mathrm{CO}-\) (a carbon atom joined to an oxygen atom by a double bond, between two carbon atoms).

(b) (i) Ethanol to ethene is dehydration. Ethanol heated at 443 K with excess concentrated sulphuric acid, which acts as the dehydrating agent, loses a water molecule:

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{hot conc. } H_2SO_4,\ 443\ K} CH_2{=}CH_2 + H_2O}\)

(ii) Ethanol to ethanoic acid is oxidation. It needs an oxidising agent such as alkaline potassium permanganate or acidified potassium dichromate, and heating:

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH + 2[O] \xrightarrow{\text{alkaline } KMnO_4,\ \text{heat}} CH_3COOH + H_2O}\)

rows.stem:
(a) Name two cyclic hydrocarbons and draw the structure of any one.

(b) Explain the process of micelle formation on adding soap in water.
rows.solution:
(a) Any two cyclic hydrocarbons: cyclohexane, \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}}\), and benzene, \(\mathrm{C_6H_6}\).

Structure of cyclohexane: six carbon atoms joined by single bonds in a closed ring (a hexagon), each carbon carrying two hydrogen atoms.

(Benzene: six carbon atoms in a ring with single and double bonds alternating around it, each carbon carrying one hydrogen atom.)

(b) A soap molecule is the sodium (or potassium) salt of a long-chain carboxylic acid. Its two ends behave differently: the ionic end is hydrophilic and dissolves in water, while the long hydrocarbon tail is hydrophobic and dissolves in oil.

In water, the soap molecules arrange themselves in clusters with their hydrocarbon tails pointing inwards, away from the water, and their ionic ends on the outside facing the water. Such a cluster is a micelle. Oily dirt collects in the centre of the micelle, among the tails. The micelles stay suspended in the water as an emulsion, so the dirt is pulled out of the cloth and rinsed away.
